## What it does
GFP is a jellyfish protein that glows green. It catches blue light energy from a partner protein called aequorin and gives it back out as green light [UniProt].

## The parts that matter
Three building blocks in the middle of the chain, positions 65 to 67, fuse together into a tiny light-emitting ring [UniProt]. The rest of the protein folds around it like a protective can [AlphaFold DB].

## What goes wrong when it breaks
The databases list no diseases for GFP. Its job is simply to glow, and that depends on the ring at positions 65 to 67 [UniProt].
